title: Modular forms — Hecke theory, newforms, and L-functions, Part II: GL₂ automorphic representations and transfer
summary: Complete target-level follow-up of the fifteen canonical R17.6 nodes in the accepted R17.3 packet. Imports retain all identifiers; replacement field records give the three dyadic calculations, corrected Katz supplier contracts and conditional transfer interfaces. Three classical-form input targets move down from the later Galois roadmap under the binding tier rule. The plan is planned, not closed: two geometric proof gaps, a Katz auxiliary-level removal gap and three R15.2 supplier requests remain; seven existing upstream-layer contracts are imported.

nodes.title: The classical newform eigencomponent
nodes.statement: For a normalized primitive cuspidal eigenform f of integer weight k≥2, exact level M and character χ, let K_f include all a_n(f) and χ-values, and choose λ|2. Construct the two-dimensional K_{f,λ}-space V_{f,λ} with its continuous G_Q action and commuting scalar Hecke action. For k=2 it is the λ-factor of V₂(A_f), importing the actual modular quotient and its rank from R14.5. For k≥3 it is the dual of the f-component of rational geometric parabolic H¹ with Sym^{k−2}R¹π_* coefficients, using the Hecke action compared with classical a_q(f). At small levels use an auxiliary full level n≥3 divisible by M and take the finite-level invariants that recover Γ₁(M), before selecting the primitive f-component. The finite-level descent is Galois-equivariant, includes the cyclotomic descent datum and retains χ; it is not invariants only under an SL₂ deck group on one geometric component. Changes of auxiliary level give canonical Hecke/Galois-equivariant isomorphisms. No Chow-motive category or integral idempotent is asserted.
hypotheses: f is primitive at its stated exact level, not an arbitrary oldform eigenvector.
The scalar field is K_{f,λ}; finite extensions of it are allowed and recorded.
Cohomology is rational when the Hecke projector is taken; denominators are not assumed invertible in an integral lattice.
proofSteps: Import the geometric relative coefficient system, its parabolic image and the comparison of Hecke actions from the named R14.3 nodes.
For weight two, use the actual quotient A_f and rational Tate exactness/rank two; take the chosen λ-factor, without asserting integral Tate exactness.

For k≥3, compare parabolic Betti cohomology with cuspidal forms, use semisimplicity of the rational good-prime Hecke algebra and primitive multiplicity one to isolate f, and transport the component to étale cohomology. Scholl §4.2.0 includes the upper-triangular GL₂(Z/n) invariants and the auxiliary-level correction.

Dualize the contravariant cohomological realization to put arithmetic Frobenius in the newform normalization; finite étale descent and trace/pullback identify auxiliary-level choices. The existence of the higher-weight rank-two projector/comparison is retained as G1, not inferred from the weight-two comparison.
acceptance: The module has dimension two, not the dimension of the entire modular-curve cohomology.
The k=2 realization agrees with the supplied A_f Tate factor.
Record whether arithmetic or geometric Frobenius is used before comparing a characteristic polynomial.

nodes.title: Galois representations of classical newforms
nodes.statement: For the preceding primitive f of weight k≥2, exact level M, character χ and chosen λ|2, V_{f,λ} carries a continuous two-dimensional representation ρ_{f,λ}, unramified at all q∤2M. For arithmetic Frobenius at such q its characteristic polynomial is X²−a_q(f)X+χ(q)q^{k−1}. Its determinant character is χ·ε₂^{k−1}. After a finite coefficient extension choose a stable lattice; reduction followed by semisimplification is a continuous finite-image residual representation. Its full good-prime characteristic polynomials are the reductions of these polynomials. Up to a common residue-field extension the residual semisimplification is independent of the chosen lattice. The statement requires no condition 2≥k and no ordinary/crystalline condition at 2.
hypotheses: K_f contains χ-values and the coefficient prime λ lies over 2.
Arithmetic Frobenius and the arithmetic normalized Hecke operators are used.
Residual comparisons specify the extension of λ and the embeddings into a common algebraic residue field.
proofSteps: Use classical-eigencomponent to construct the action and good reduction away from 2M; in weight two import special-fibre Eichler–Shimura.

For k≥3 use the coefficient correspondence trace and the decomposition of the good-prime isogeny correspondence into Frobenius and Verschiebung (Deligne Proposition 3.18, §4.6–Theorem 4.9). On the weight-k coefficient system, FV=q^{k−1}, and T_q=F+⟨q⟩V. Scholl §4.2.2 also uses duality/conjugation to ensure both polynomial roots occur; merely annihilating a two-dimensional space by that polynomial is insufficient. G1 records the remaining higher-weight geometric proof input.
Compare geometric Frobenius on cohomology with arithmetic Frobenius on its dual. Identify the determinant globally by good-prime density and continuous character recognition.

Apply the R01 stable-lattice and reduction nodes. Chebotarev and the full-polynomial recognition node give lattice independence and comparison with the supplied residual representation. DS Theorem 6.1 is the statement, not a proof of the geometric input; §§6.12–6.13 supply the residual comparison.
acceptance: Good-prime trace and determinant both agree; trace alone in characteristic two is insufficient.
Weight two has determinant χ(q)q, and weight five has determinant χ(q)q⁴.
No weight-one attached-representation existence is taken as a prerequisite: the dihedral Artin representation is already given by quadratic induction.
No global absolute-irreducibility or semisimplicity theorem for the characteristic-zero realization is required here; residual reduction is explicitly semisimplified.

sources.match: Classical and residual representations; the higher-weight geometric theorem is treated as an input in this source.

nodes.title: The odd residual conductor bound
nodes.statement: Let f, λ|2 and ρ_{f,λ} be as in classical-galois-realization, and let r̄_{f,λ} be the semisimplified stable-lattice reduction. For every odd prime q, a_q(r̄_{f,λ})≤a_q(ρ_{f,λ})=v_q(M), hence the prime-to-two Artin conductor N(r̄_{f,λ}) divides M^(2), the odd part of the exact newform level. This uses local compatibility only at q≠2. Equality for the residual conductor is not asserted. A finite-order characteristic-zero twist is tracked on both the automorphic and Galois sides before applying the conductor-preserving local correspondence.
hypotheses: The form is primitive at exact level M.
Artin conductors are taken for full representations, not just determinants.
q is different from the residual characteristic 2, so R01’s reduction inequality applies.
proofSteps: Apply the rank-two local newvector/conductor comparison and Carayol’s classical local comparison at odd q. In Carayol’s convention the Weil representation uses geometric reciprocity and a dual/unitary twist; translate to the arithmetic normalization fixed above. Unramified dual/absolute-value twists do not change inertia or the Artin conductor.

For odd q, the local comparison has the principal-series, special, and ordinary (quadratically induced) cuspidal cases. Carayol §§11.1–11.3 reduce the ordinary case to a global induced character with the same local component. The special case requires nonzero monodromy, not just equality of semisimplifications; §11.4 identifies its image using Picard–Lefschetz. G2 retains the proof of this geometric comparison at Q, rather than importing its later higher-roadmap statement.

Use the existing R01 reduction and semisimplification inequalities prime by prime. Multiply the odd-prime inequalities to obtain divisibility. Do not use Carayol §12.3’s extraordinary dyadic cubic argument.
acceptance: Conductor may strictly decrease on reduction; equality must not be a test.
If a constructed congruent primitive form has odd level M|N(r̄), divisibility forces M=N(r̄).
Unramified twists preserve the odd local conductor; a ramified determinant twist does not automatically preserve the exact level.

sources.match: Odd-prime local comparison with normalization and special monodromy retained; extraordinary dyadic §12.3 is excluded.

nodeRefinements.statement: A continuous absolutely irreducible r̄:G_Q→GL₂(F̄₂) with solvable projective image has projective image D_n of order 2n, for an odd n≥3. Its finite image is a central extension by a cyclic odd-order scalar group, so projective solvability implies linear solvability. The quadratic field cut out by the rotation subgroup is the inducing field after determinant normalization.
hypotheses: F̄₂ has the discrete topology; continuity makes the image finite.
Absolute irreducibility is required, not just nontriviality.
proofSteps: Factor through a finite Galois quotient. Apply the existing finite subgroup/dihedral induction classification from R01.4.

Scalar kernels are abelian, so pass from solvable projective to solvable linear image. The characteristic-two irreducible solvable classification rules out the Borel case (a normal 2-group fixes a line), cyclic diagonalizable image, and the nonsolvable PSL₂ cases.
The determinant normalization has the same projective image and trivial scalar intersection in SL₂; its image is the actual D_n.
acceptance: D_1 and cyclic images are reducible; n≥3 is explicit.
A reducible upper-triangular solvable representation is a non-example.
No claim that arbitrary solvable Galois restriction preserves irreducibility.

nodeRefinements.statement: For finite-image r̄ in characteristic two, det r̄ has odd finite order and has a unique square-root character ξ. The twist r̄₀=ξ⁻¹⊗r̄ has determinant one, the same projective image and irreducibility, and no nonidentity scalar in its image. The finite scalar character ξ is unramified at 2. If the projective image is D_n with n odd, the image of r̄₀ is linearly D_n. Twist a characteristic-zero modular lift back by the Teichmüller Dirichlet lift of ξ, and record its actual new level and character rather than asserting an unchanged minimal level.
hypotheses: The character is lifted at the chosen prime over 2.
Projective dihedral means n odd≥3 here.
proofSteps: Inverse Frobenius on F̄₂× supplies the unique square root, compatibly with multiplication. In any finite coefficient field its order is odd.
The determinant of a scalar in rank two is its square; in characteristic two a square equal to one forces the scalar to be one.

Local reciprocity for Q₂ sends the pro-2 unit group to a finite group of odd order trivially; global Kronecker–Weber/class field theory identifies the finite character with a Dirichlet character of odd conductor.
Apply the classical newform twist operation, extending coefficient field and the prime when necessary. Compare full residual polynomials and include the changed level in the witness.
acceptance: A nontrivial odd-order determinant is allowed.
The normalized linear image injects into its projective image.
Untwisting is an algebraic operation and is not a proof of modularity or of level preservation.

sources.match: Normalization needed to apply the source’s linear-dihedral theorem.
The broader projective-dihedral lift allows a scalar twist; its coefficients/prime must be tracked.
The odd-order square root of the determinant is unramified at 2 by Kronecker–Weber; this local character argument is used without importing the general weight/level-lowering theorem.

nodeRefinements.statement: For linearly dihedral r̄₀=Ind_{G_K}^{G_Q}φ of determinant one and rotation order n odd, let D be the fundamental discriminant of K and φ̃ its same-order Teichmüller lift at λ|2. Then the finite Artin lift ρ=Ind φ̃ has conductor |D| Norm(f_{φ̃})=2^νN(r̄₀). At each odd prime the conductor is unchanged on reduction. The dyadic possibilities are: (i) D odd and Norm(f) odd, ν=0; (ii) D≡5 mod8 and Norm(f)≡4 mod8, ν=2; (iii) D≡4 mod8 and Norm(f) odd, ν=2; (iv) 8|D and Norm(f) odd, ν=3. Rohrlich–Tunnell’s exact theorem uses (i), (ii) and (iv), not (iii).
hypotheses: φ has odd finite order and φ^σ=φ⁻¹.
D is the signed fundamental discriminant and |D| is used in the positive conductor.
The Teichmüller lift is taken at the fixed residue embedding.
proofSteps: Import the quadratic-induction conductor formula. Teichmüller preserves the kernel of the odd-order rotation character.

For odd-prime inertia subgroups, compute fixed dimensions separately for rotations, a reflection, and noncyclic dihedral subgroups. In characteristic zero a reflection has ±1 eigenvalues; its reduction is a nonidentity unipotent with one-dimensional fixed space. Both noncyclic cases have no common fixed line. Repeat for ramification subgroups, not only tame inertia.
At 2, odd-order characters kill principal pro-2 units. Split or ramified quadratic residue field F₂ gives no unit character; inert residue field F₄ permits conductor norm 4. Combine with v₂(D)=0,2,3.
acceptance: A characteristic-two reflection has trace zero but is not the identity.
Case (iii) is present in the conductor classification and absent from the exact RT modularity theorem.
Positive discriminant D≡3 mod8 cannot be a fundamental odd discriminant; interpret the source’s sign notation through the field splitting cases.

sources.match: Conductor classification and its retained dyadic cases.
Kernel-preserving odd-order lift and conductor comparison.

nodeRefinements.statement: Let g=Σb(n)q^n be a normalized primitive cuspidal weight-one form of exact level 2^νNr and character χ with χ²=1, N odd and ν∈{0,2,3}. Let λ|2, with residual representation the given quadratic-induced Artin lift’s reduction r̄ and N=N(r̄). Here r=1 or an odd prime not dividing N; for r≠1 require b(r) modλ≠1. For ν=2 require b(n)=0 for every even n. For ν=3 require b(2) modλ≠0. Then a primitive form f of exact odd level N and trivial character gives the same residual semisimplified representation: its weight is 2 if ν=0 or 2, and 4 if ν=3. The coefficient field and prime may be extended. No general weight-one attached-representation theorem is needed when the Artin representation is supplied by induction.
hypotheses: All Fourier coefficients used in the constructions are λ-integral; reduction is in a specified common finite field.
The χ²=1 character reduces to the trivial character at λ|2.
The integral trace identity is proved before reducing any expression with denominators.
proofSteps: For ν=0, square g. Its mod-2 q-expansion is Σb(n)²q^{2n}; inverse coefficient Frobenius gives the away-two eigenpacket of g at weight two. Choose a common eigenvector for the remaining commuting operators inside the nonzero away-two eigenspace, allowing a finite residue extension, then use R15.5 lifting for the full Hecke algebra; the T₂ eigenvalue is not claimed unchanged.

For ν=2, write m=Nr. The even-coefficient vanishing gives g|C=−g for C=(1,0;2m,1), via W_{4m}(1,−1/2;0,1)W_{4m}^{−1}; thus g² has level 2m. Choose 4a+mb=1. The three-coset trace and the determinant-four partial Atkin–Lehner matrix J=(4,1;−4mb,4a) yield h=2λ_J^{−2}Tr(g²) at level m, with integral q-coefficients and reduction Σb(n)²q^n. The specific local Atkin–Li input gives λ_J=±1 here; this is not an assertion for arbitrary nontrivial character. Apply inverse coefficient Frobenius and R15.5.

For ν=3, U₄(g²) is weight two of level 2m and has nonzero residual away-two packet because b(2) is a unit. Lift to a primitive weight-two g₁ with level dividing 2N after removing r. If its level is odd, square g₁. If it is 2L with L|N odd, use the determinant-two matrix J=(2,1;−2Lb,4a), 4a+Lb=1, and the three-coset trace of g₁². Twice the trace is integral with expansion Σc₁(2n)q^n+2Σc₁(n)q^n, and reduces to Σb₁(n)²q^n. Lift at weight four and level dividing N.

Use the source slash convention F∥_kγ=det(γ)^{k/2}(cz+d)^{−k}F(γz). Tau Ceti’s arithmetic slash has det(γ)^{k−1}; multiply by det(γ)^{1−k/2} before using these identities. The positive square root is taken for positive determinant.

Remove an auxiliary r by the trivial-character weight-two newform condition a_r=±1 when r divides its level exactly once: its eigenvalue is congruent to b(r)≠1. Finally full good-prime polynomials identify residual semisimplifications; classical-residual-conductor-bound and M|N force M=N.
acceptance: Keep ν=3 separate: its asserted output weight is four.
Inverse coefficient Frobenius is not the identity unless the coefficient field is F₂.
Do not reduce 1/2 terms before the integral trace identity.
Exact level N follows from both divisibilities, not merely from a trace construction.

sources.match: The three integral trace constructions, the removal of r, and the residual conductor argument, with all dyadic conditions retained.

nodeRefinements.statement: For the real inducing quadratic K in RT cases (i), (ii) or (iv), there is an odd quadratic-induced Artin lift of level 2^νNr satisfying the technical lemma, with r an auxiliary odd split rational prime away from 2N and residual b(r)≠1. A quadratic character ξ_K, ramified at exactly one real place and the chosen degree-one prime 𝔯, and unramified at 2, changes the signature and reduces trivially mod2. Its induction is odd, has the required χ²=1 and preserves the stated dyadic coefficient conditions.
hypotheses: Use a narrow ray class modulus 4f and an odd-order character φ̃.
The auxiliary prime is chosen in the RT signature class, not the Wiese Frobenius-identity class.
proofSteps: In the narrow ray class group, split off the odd-order part and choose a class on which φ̃ is nontrivial, then combine it with the mixed-signature class. Chebotarev gives a degree-one prime 𝔯 in that class away from the forbidden primes.
For an odd exponent n, arrange 𝔯^n=(ρ) with mixed real signs and ρ≡1 mod4f. The extension K(√ρ)/K yields ξ_K. Its local properties follow from the ray congruence and the odd valuation at 𝔯.

Apply the induction conductor formula and quadratic-induction automorphy. The split r has residual trace different from one, unlike the primes used to kill a U-operator in Wiese’s argument. In ν=2 the relevant local ramification forces all even coefficients to vanish; in ν=3 the local factor makes b(2) a unit.

The rational auxiliary prime is split and coprime to 2N.
Do not interchange this b(r)≠1 construction with Wiese’s trace-zero auxiliary primes.

nodeRefinements.statement: Let r̄:G_Q→GL₂(F̄₂) be continuous absolutely irreducible with LINEAR image D_n of order 2n, n odd≥3. Let K be its quadratic inducing field, D its fundamental discriminant and N its prime-to-two Artin conductor. If D is odd or divisible by 8, r̄ is realized by a primitive cuspidal form of exact level N and trivial character, of weight two when D is odd and weight four when 8|D. The form, coefficient field, a chosen prime λ|2, lattice and residual isomorphism form the R15.6 witness. The claim does not include D≡4 mod8 or a projective-dihedral representation with a nontrivial scalar determinant.
hypotheses: Linear dihedral image, rather than only projective dihedral image.
The representation is supplied over a finite residue field embedded in F̄₂.
proofSteps: Apply teichmuller-conductor to separate cases (i), (ii), (iv). Correct the inherited source case label E1.
For imaginary K, the same-order lift is already odd; for real K use serre-odd-trick. Apply the technical lemma at the actual ν and N.

Package the form and all coefficient/prime/lattice choices as the existing witness. For a general scalar twist return to determinant-untwist, but no longer claim this exact level/character conclusion.
acceptance: Both odd D cases, including the inert-at-two ν=2 lift, yield weight two.
8|D yields weight four.
D≡4 mod8 is a non-example of the theorem’s hypotheses, not a missing subcase of its proof.

sources.locator: Theorem and cases (i)–(iv), p.307; proof pp.307–308
sources.match: Exact linear-dihedral conductor, weight and discriminant hypotheses.

nodeRefinements.statement: Every continuous absolutely irreducible projective-dihedral mod-2 representation of G_Q has an odd finite-image characteristic-zero quadratic-induced lift, integral over a cyclotomic coefficient ring at a specified prime above 2, whose reduction is the given representation. Without unramifiedness at 2, this assertion controls neither its conductor nor its minimal weight. If the residual representation is unramified at 2, either the same-level lift is odd, or infinitely many auxiliary split primes ℓ give odd lifts of conductor Nℓ with residual Frob_ℓ the identity (hence trace zero), where N is the odd residual conductor.
hypotheses: The inducing character and its conjugate are distinct; the scalar character is retained.
The cyclotomic coefficient field and prime above 2 are part of the construction.
For the Nℓ alternative require residual unramifiedness at 2 and use the strengthened modulus 4D f σ(f).
proofSteps: Lift the inducing odd-order character by Teichmüller at the chosen prime. If the induction is even, K is real; twist the inducing lift by a quadratic character with mixed real signature, whose reduction is trivial. This proves the unrestricted existence assertion.

For the unramified-at-two conductor assertion, impose the ray congruence simultaneously for f and its conjugate σ(f), using inherited E6’s repair. Chebotarev then supplies split primes at which BOTH diagonal inducing characters are trivial.
Choose the signature-changing quadratic character ramified only at one real place and one degree-one prime above ℓ, and unramified at 2. The quadratic-induction conductor formula gives Nℓ.
acceptance: Frob_ℓ identity is proved from two trivial characters, not merely from splitting in K.
The residual identity has trace zero in characteristic two.
No arbitrary-conductor lift is used as if it were a same-level Katz form.

sources.match: Unramified conductor-controlled and unrestricted odd-lift assertions are separate; E6 supplies the conjugate modulus.

nodeRefinements.statement: For a continuous absolutely irreducible projective-dihedral r̄:G_Q→GL₂(F̄₂) unramified at 2, there exists a normalized cuspidal full-Hecke eigenform in the Katz space of weight one, level N=N(r̄) odd, and character det r̄ (with its prime-to-two Dirichlet interpretation). It has the good-prime residual characteristic polynomials of r̄. A finite coefficient-field extension is allowed. Scalar or nonsemisimple Frobenius at 2 is included. A characteristic-zero weight-one form at that same level is not asserted.
hypotheses: Katz cusp conditions are imposed at every cusp.
All T_q, the appropriate bad U-operators and diamonds are included in the eigenform conclusion.
The two requested R15.2 oldform and independence/descent contracts are prerequisites.
Level N names the Katz carrier at the residual conductor; this node asserts no separate Katz primitivity/minimality predicate.
proofSteps: Apply wiese-odd-lift. If its odd lift has conductor N, use quadratic-induction weight-one modularity and reduction. Otherwise, for infinitely many ℓ, obtain lifts at Nℓ.
Use Wiese Proposition 4/Corollary 5 to raise two powers and impose U_ℓ=0 at Nℓ³; the companion matrix works also with repeated roots. After reduction, coefficients at indices divisible by ℓ vanish.

Use the fixed finite group of the characteristic-zero monomial lifts to bound the possibilities at the finitely many primes dividing N, in a common finite residual coefficient field. The good-prime polynomials, including q=2, are fixed by r̄. Select distinct ℓ₁,ℓ₂ with matching prime coefficients. This gives agreement at primes only, not equality of all q-expansion coefficients.

The published comparison fails at ℓ₁²: U_{ℓ₁}g₁=0 gives a_{ℓ₁²}(g₁)=0, whereas g₂ is good at ℓ₁ with a_{ℓ₁}(g₂)=0 and determinant/character 1, hence a_{ℓ₁²}(g₂)=0²−1=1 in characteristic two. Proposition 7 pullback preserves these coefficients. Gap G3 requires a valid auxiliary-level removal argument before Proposition 7/Corollary 8 can descend an independent form to N, retaining cusps, character and the required full eigenpacket. Stabilizing both primes alone does not establish independence.
acceptance: The Q(√229) class-group example gives an unramified dyadic reflection: its matrix is a nonidentity unipotent although its semisimplification is scalar.
No hypothesis of two distinct dyadic Frobenius eigenvalues is added.
No same-level characteristic-zero weight-one lift is substituted for Katz weight one.
Agreement of every prime coefficient does not imply agreement at auxiliary prime powers; explicitly test the ℓ₁² discrepancy 0≠1.
The G3 replacement must include scalar and nonsemisimple Frobenius at 2 and must not assume auxiliary-level independence from zero U-eigenvalues.

nodeRefinements.statement: Every continuous absolutely irreducible mod-2 representation of G_Q with solvable projective image has a residual modularity witness arising from a characteristic-zero cuspidal weight-one primitive form. The actual level, character, coefficient field, prime above 2, stable lattice and isomorphism after common residue extension are recorded. There is no assertion of prescribed minimal weight or level in this general existence statement.

The odd lift and its weight-one modular form have matching full good-prime polynomials.

Apply R17.5’s quadratic-induction automorphy and Q weight-one comparison, which retain the supplied Artin representation.

Choose a primitive form in the same packet and record its actual data. Compare reduction using full characteristic polynomials and R01 recognition; the already-given induced representation supplies the finite lift, avoiding a later-roadmap weight-one existence prerequisite.
acceptance: Scalar determinants are permitted.
The specific λ is part of the witness.
Distinguish the unrestricted existence conclusion from the RT exact-level theorem.

nodeRefinements.statement: The preceding residual witness can be replaced by one of weight at least two, with its actual new weight, primitive level M, character, coefficient field and chosen prime over 2 recorded. One unconditional characteristic-zero route multiplies the integral weight-one form by E₄≡1 mod2, obtains a weight-five residual eigenpacket, and applies R15.5 to produce a characteristic-zero primitive form of weight five at level dividing the input level. For a Katz weight-one form, multiplication by the p=2 Hasse invariant A of weight one gives weight two with the same q-expansion. Deligne–Serre lifting at weight two is allowed only when Af belongs to the reduction of the required finite-free integral cusp-form module; otherwise use a justified Hasse power/auxiliary level for which cusp-sheaf H¹ vanishes and record the resulting weight and level. The historical node id is not an unconditional weight-two assertion.

A Katz section is not automatically a reduction of a characteristic-zero vector.
All commuting Hecke operators used to select a normalized primitive form are included; eigenvalues, not a prescribed vector, lift.

The initial weight-changed section is only guaranteed to be an eigenvector away from 2. Simultaneous diagonalizability is not assumed; finite commutative-algebra eigenvector selection precedes full-algebra lifting.

The weight change preserves the common away-two Hecke eigensystem. On the nonzero away-two eigenspace in the finite-dimensional reduction of the actual finite-free integral module, choose a common eigenvector for the remaining commuting T₂/bad U/diamond operators after a finite residue extension. Its eigenvalue at 2 need not equal that of the weight-one form. Apply DS to this full commuting algebra, extend the coefficient prime, then normalize and select a primitive constituent of level dividing the input level. Use classical-galois-realization and full good-prime polynomial recognition away from 2.

For the Katz route, A has q-expansion one and weight p−1=1. State the exact cusp-sheaf base-change hypothesis before DS. If it is not available at Γ₁(N), pass to full auxiliary odd level n≥3, choose a high enough Hasse power to make the cusp-sheaf H¹ vanish, then use the supplied integral module and DS. The R15.2 full-level theorem is not a Γ₁(N) weight-two theorem.
Return the existing witness at the output form’s actual primitive level and chosen extended prime.

A at p=2 shifts one to two, but does not by itself prove classical liftability.
The coefficient prime and any auxiliary level are recorded.
No general minimal-weight level lowering is imported through this interface.
Multiplication by E₄ or A need not preserve the T₂ eigenvalue; matching the residual representation uses the odd good primes.

The Γ₁(N) classicality qualification N≥5, not an all-level shortcut.

nodeRefinements.statement: Let F be a number field and r̄:G_F→GL₂(k) continuous absolutely irreducible with finite projective image. Let M/F be the finite Galois extension cut out by its projective kernel. If a finite extension E/F is linearly disjoint from M, then r̄|_{G_E} has the same projective image and is absolutely irreducible. Disjointness from the extension cut out by the full linear kernel is a sufficient stronger condition. E/F need not be Galois for this restriction statement.

Disjointness is from the actual projective-kernel field, not an arbitrary auxiliary extension.

A line is invariant under a matrix exactly when it is invariant under its projective class; the same projective image has precisely the same invariant lines.
For a stronger full-kernel field, surjectivity gives equal linear image and the existing Representation.IsIrreducible formulation applies directly.

Solvability alone is not a disjointness hypothesis.
The statement is unchanged by scalar twists.

nodeRefinements.statement: Let r=Ind_{G_K}^{G_F}θ be absolutely irreducible over an algebraically closed field, with K/F quadratic and θ≠θ^σ. For a finite E/F, r|_{G_E} is absolutely irreducible exactly when K is not contained in E and θ|_{G_{EK}}≠θ^σ|_{G_{EK}}. If K⊂E it splits into the two restricted characters. If K⊄E, restriction is the index-two induction from EK/E; its two eigenlines are exchanged when the restricted characters differ. This criterion holds in characteristic two without Maschke.

Characters are compared on the actual subgroup G_{EK}.
proofSteps: Use the existing Mackey decomposition over arbitrary coefficient rings, followed by the direct index-two character argument from R01.4.
When the characters differ, a stable line for their diagonal action must be one of the two eigenlines, and an element outside the index-two subgroup swaps those lines.

When they agree, over an algebraically closed field extend the common character using a root of the square of a coset representative; Frobenius reciprocity gives a one-dimensional quotient and reducibility. In characteristic two that square root still exists, even though the induction need not split semisimply.
The pinned characteristic-zero Mackey irreducibility theorem is a checked boundary, not a valid premise for this characteristic-two proof.
acceptance: Containing K forces reducibility.
Distinct characters before restriction can become equal after restriction.
An equal-character index-two induction in characteristic two can be nonsplit and remains reducible.

sources.match: Quadratic-induced matrix description; the restriction criterion is an application of the generic induction owner.

nodeRefinements.statement: Let E/F be finite solvable Galois with a prime-cyclic tower. Supply a rank-two compatible family ρ_λ over F and a cuspidal GL₂ representation π whose arithmetic-normalized good local polynomials match that family. At each cyclic step take the R17.4 base change and impose its exact no-self-twist criterion for cuspidality. Then the iterated base change matches ρ_λ|_{G_E}: at a good v and w|v of residue degree f, the roots α_v,β_v become α_v^f,β_v^f, and the determinant becomes (α_vβ_v)^f. Residual absolute irreducibility is preserved when E is disjoint from the projective-kernel field, or when the explicit quadratic criterion holds at all steps. Existence of the family and of its coefficient field is supplied data, not proved by automorphic base change.
hypotheses: Exclude a finite set containing the ramification of the family and π; record whether E/F is ramified locally.
Use arithmetic Frobenius and the normalized local dictionary consistently.
Cuspidality is checked at every cyclic step, not inferred from solvability of E/F.
proofSteps: Apply R17.4 prime-cyclic transfer successively; use its tower-independence and all-place local compatibility.
The local norm sends a uniformizer at w to valuation f at v, so an unramified parameter has roots raised to f even at a ramified local extension. q_w=q_v^f.

The restricted compatible family has those same full good polynomials. Apply the existing recognition theorem when its semisimplicity hypotheses hold, and separately use the residual restriction criteria.
acceptance: For α=2, β=3 and f=2, the new trace is 13 and determinant 36, not trace 25.
Self-twist may make a base change noncuspidal.
No arbitrary nonsolvable extension is covered.

nodeRefinements.statement: For cyclic E/F of prime degree ℓ and a cuspidal Π invariant under Gal(E/F), the cuspidal descents are exactly ℓ distinct forms π⊗η^i (0≤i<ℓ), where η cuts out E/F. Supply their rank-two attached compatible families and a rank-two compatible family ρ_λ over F whose restrictions are absolutely irreducible and match Π. Then the descent matching one specified member ρ_λ₀ is determined by full good-prime polynomials; the matching exponent i is independent of λ once the compared coefficient fields/embeddings are fixed and the common compatible polynomials agree. Determinants alone do not choose it when ℓ=2. Iterate only with this data and criterion at each prime-cyclic step.
hypotheses: Π is cuspidal and Galois invariant.
The restricted Galois members are absolutely irreducible; the families of the descents are supplied.
A fixed common coefficient field and embeddings permit equality of good polynomials to be transported between λ.
proofSteps: Import R17.4 cyclic descent and its fiber theorem. It has exactly ℓ distinct descents; invariance alone does not specify one of them.
Schur’s lemma makes any two extensions of the same absolutely irreducible restricted representation differ by a character of Gal(E/F), yielding η^i at a chosen λ.

Good-prime polynomial equality in the common coefficient field transports the same i to every λ; use full-polynomial recognition with its semisimplicity hypotheses. Strong multiplicity one yields uniqueness of the matching cuspidal descent.
Record each intermediate descent and twist in a solvable tower; no canonical choice is inferred merely from the existence of an extension.
acceptance: A quadratic twist in the kernel has the same determinant as π’s representation; determinant alone is a failure test.
If restriction is reducible, the Schur argument and uniqueness criterion do not apply.
At each stage the selected i is the same across the compatible system.

Require absolute irreducibility of every intermediate restriction (for example via projective-kernel disjointness) and attached compatible families for the intermediate descents. Then the compatible-descent criterion selects matching cuspidal descents step by step to F, with the stated local base-change compatibility and one coefficient-compatible twist at each step. Galois invariance of Π follows from the extending family and strong multiplicity one. No potential modularity existence theorem, coefficient-independent attachment theorem, or nonnormal cubic descent is asserted.

Prescribed local behavior and linear disjointness are explicit inputs supplied by the extension-construction owner.
Matching means full normalized good local polynomials, with all relevant fields and embeddings recorded.

Apply compatible-descent along the chosen tower, maintaining cuspidality and absolute irreducibility. Choose the character ambiguity using the common compatible polynomials.

Apply compatible-base-change for local comparisons, retaining any local types supplied by the all-place R17.4 dictionary. The extension-construction theorem and modularity-lifting theorem remain external consumers, not newly planned here.

A solvable extension containing K may violate residual irreducibility.
Potential modularity does not automatically imply modularity over F without these descent inputs.

On V_ℓ^i f=f(q^{ℓ^i}), i=0,…,r, r≥1, U_ℓ has companion matrix with first row (a_ℓ,1,0,…), second row (−δℓ^{k−1}ε(ℓ),0,1,…), subsequent superdiagonal ones, and characteristic polynomial X^{r−1}(X²−a_ℓX+δℓ^{k−1}ε(ℓ)). δ=1 if ℓ∤N and 0 otherwise. Import the Mackey restriction/decomposition and Frobenius reciprocity formulas over the actual representation/FDRep carriers in arbitrary characteristic. The index-two eigenline proof supplies irreducibility in characteristic two; no Maschke assumption is introduced.

G2: complete the Q odd-prime local geometric comparison, including nonzero special monodromy, using the lower geometric suppliers; no extraordinary dyadic cubic comparison.

At assembly, apply all same-id refinements and the three ownership moves before rechecking the combined graph and the six-planet budget. The prime coefficients agree but their ℓ₁² coefficients are 0 and 1, so Proposition 7 cannot identify the pullbacks. Prove the required independence or give a different valid level-removal construction, preserving cusp conditions at every cusp, character det r̄ and the full required good-prime polynomials/Hecke packet, including T₂ and scalar or nonsemisimple dyadic Frobenius.
